title: Secure Boot — ASUS notebook
text: Select the outlined Secure Boot Control option, then choose Disabled. The status above it can update only after saving and restarting.
menu: Security → Secure Boot → Secure Boot Control

title: Secure Boot — ASUS desktop
text: On this ASUS layout, choose Other OS in the outlined menu to deactivate Secure Boot. Keep the PC in UEFI boot mode; Other OS here is a Secure Boot control.

title: Fast Boot — ASUS UEFI
text: Open Boot, select the outlined Fast Boot row, and choose Disabled. This is the firmware setting, separate from Windows Fast Startup.

title: Intel virtualization — ASUS motherboard
text: The yellow outline marks the setting to change. This reference screenshot shows Enabled: change it to Disabled for this setup. The read-only Intel VT-x Technology: Supported line above is not the switch.

title: Intel CPU + VT-d — MSI Click BIOS X
target: Intel Virtualization Tech + Intel VT-D Tech → Disabled
text: The outlines mark two separate controls. Choose Disabled for Intel Virtualization Tech, then change Intel VT-D Tech separately. The open dropdown in this reference image covers the VT-d value; check both controls on your own PC.

title: AMD virtualization — ASUS notebook
text: The yellow outline marks SVM Mode, the AMD CPU virtualization switch. This example shows Enabled: change it to Disabled for this setup. If your firmware also exposes IOMMU, check that separately using your model’s manual.

title: Save changes — ASUS notebook
text: After completing all BIOS changes, save and confirm the restart. This ASUS example outlines OK; other models may call it Yes, Apply or Save Changes and Exit.
menu: Save & Exit, or press F10 after completing all changes

title: Secure Boot — Gigabyte / AORUS AM4
text: Open Advanced Mode → Boot → Secure Boot. Select the yellow-outlined Secure Boot control, then choose Disabled. This AM4 reference shows Enabled and Active before the change; Active is a status, not the setting to select. Keep UEFI boot mode. The Custom mode and key-management items visible in this source picture are not steps to follow for this setup.
credit: Gigabyte AM4 / sTRX4 Secure Boot reference

title: Secure Boot — ASRock X300TM-ITX
text: Open the Security tab, then select the outlined Secure Boot entry. This screenshot shows the entry that opens its settings, not the on/off control itself. In the following screen, set Secure Boot to Disabled. The password rows are separate controls. This is the X300TM-ITX layout; check your model’s manual if it differs.

title: AMD SVM + IOMMU — ASRock X300TM-ITX
text: Open Advanced → CPU Configuration. Change the first outlined row, SVM Mode, to Disabled. Then change IOMMU separately to Disabled. This source screenshot shows SVM Enabled and IOMMU Auto; neither is the target for this setup. PSS Support, NX Mode, SMT Mode and AMD fTPM switch are different settings.
